mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5pp does not correlate with weakening labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns do not show a significant negative trend following a sustained decline in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with supply-side contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it signals an accommodative monetary policy in a weak economic environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and negative GDPC1 growth does not correlate with positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 200,000 does not correlate with strengthening labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decrease > 1% does not correlate with weakening consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is positive, it signals a tightening monetary policy in a growing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% in 3 months and GDPC1 growth rate > 0%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of rising FEDFUNDS and positive GDPC1 growth does not correlate with negative returns.
